content:
marina: Alert — eu-west1 GPU pool (gpu-pool-3) reporting rapid degradation. Queue backlog up ~4x, inference 503s ~28% across the hostgroup. Auto-failover partially triggered but some traffic still hitting eu-west1. Investigating.

sre-bot: [ALERT] 2026-11-12 07:12 UTC — gpu-pool-3 degraded, autoscale-errors=23, kernel-oops=5

ops-oncall: oncall here, digging into node failures. pulling k8s events and dmesg.

jon-eng: seeing oom_killer and nv_peer2peer errors on 6 nodes. suspected driver hang after kernel update last night. will collect /var/log/messages + nv logs.

alex-network: also seeing increased packet loss to object store endpoints from eu-west1 edge — storage timeouts ~15%. might be correlated with BGP churn.

luis-support: we have >10 high-priority customer tickets reporting 500s/timeout. need a status page message + ETA for customers.

sarah-cs: drafting status page now. what ETA should we give externally? keep conservative.

marina: mitigation plan: 1) divert 100% traffic off eu-west1 to eu-west2 + eu-central1 with gradual ramp to avoid cold-start surge. 2) scale up cold spare pool in eu-west2 (add ~48 GPUs in cold pool). 3) cordon + drain failing nodes and roll kernel to previous stable. 4) fallback to smaller model variants for affected customers if needed. ETA: initial mitigation 30-45m, full recovery 2-3h.

ops-oncall: kicking routing shift now.

ops-oncall: ```bash
# shift routing off eu-west1 -> eu-west2 + eu-central1
curl -X POST https://control.redwood.internal/api/v1/routing/shift \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -d '{"from":"eu-west1","to":["eu-west2","eu-central1"],"percent":100}'
```

ops-oncall: shift started, control-plane shows gradual ramp. targeting 0% to eu-west1.

sre-bot: [INFO] routing shift acknowledged, start=07:18 UTC

jon-eng: draining node gpu-node-123..127, reboots queued. grabbing dmesg and /var/log/nvidia/ for analysis.

alex-network: traced BGP flap to transit-provider X in region. contacting provider. they estimate 60-90m if manual intervention needed.

sarah-cs: proposed status page copy: "We are experiencing degraded GPU capacity in eu-west1 affecting inference latency and causing elevated errors. Traffic is being rerouted to nearby regions. We estimate partial mitigation within 45 minutes and full recovery within 3 hours. Updates every 30 minutes."

marina: approved. post it and include the incident link in support replies.

luis-support: posted to status.redwood.ai — incident id INC-20261112-01. link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20261112-01

sarah-cs: preparing canned support replies and suggested workaround (temporary model downgrade + retry/backoff) for CS to send. cc @sales for any contractual notes.

finance-bot: FYI — shifting 100% traffic to cold spares and cross-region burst will increase spend. rough estimate: +$12k over next 12h.

marina: acknowledged. prioritize availability. we'll reconcile costs after containment.

jon-eng: applied kernel rollback/patch to gpu-node-123, boot looks clean, no kernel oops so far. rolling to remaining nodes in small batch to avoid mass restart.

ops-oncall: routing telemetry: eu-west1 traffic -> 3% -> now 0. autoscaler in eu-west2 launching additional pods, warm pools warming.

sre-bot: [UPDATE] 07:45 UTC — routing complete, error rate cluster-wide down to ~5%, queue backlog reduced by ~50%.

sarah-cs: customer update sent: "We have rerouted traffic off eu-west1; latency and errors are improving. Engineers are patching affected hosts. Next update in 30 minutes: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20261112-01"

marina: thanks all. keep short, timestamped updates here. escalate to CTO if this goes beyond 6h.

ops-oncall: will post another update in 30m with telemetry (error rate, queue length, % traffic by region).

marina: final for now — recovering but monitoring.
